extracted.intended_audience: Nature authors, peer reviewers, editors, and the wider research community
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and rationale for publishing peer-review files alongside research papers in Nature, describing what will be published, how reviewer anonymity is handled, and the intended benefits for authors, reviewers and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish referees’ reports and author responses with papers
rubrics_metrics.description: From 16 June, new submissions of manuscripts that are published as research articles in Nature will automatically include a link to the reviewers’ reports and author responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until now authors could opt in; the change makes the peer-review file automatic for published research articles so that, over time, more Nature papers will include a peer-review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve reviewer anonymity unless they opt to be named
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity of the reviewers will remain anonymous, unless they choose otherwise — as happens now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer names are not revealed by default; reviewers may elect to be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the exchanges between referees and authors accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchanges between the referees and the authors will be accessible to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published peer-review file contains the back-and-forth between referees and authors to illuminate the process of producing rigorous science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase transparency and build trust in the scientific process
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in doing so is to open up what many see as the ‘black box’ of science, shedding light on how a research paper is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This serves to increase transparency and (we hope) to build trust in the scientific process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and acknowledge peer reviewers (if they choose)
rubrics_metrics.description: These discussions... should receive increased recognition, including acknowledgement of the reviewers involved, if they choose to be named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is conditional on reviewers’ choice to be named; the editorial argues for greater acknowledgment of reviewing work as part of career recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide value for early-career researchers by exposing the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: For early-career researchers, there is great value in seeing inside a process that is key to their career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making reports public helps early-career researchers learn how review and revision work in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrich science communication by publishing peer-review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Making peer-reviewer reports public also enriches science communication: it’s a chance to add to the ‘story’ of how a result is arrived at, or a conclusion supported, even if it includes only the perspectives of authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published review materials can be used to contextualize results and show the debate and evidence that shaped conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat peer-review exchanges as part of the scientific record
rubrics_metrics.description: The exchanges between authors and referees should be seen as a crucial part of the scientific record, just as they are a key part of doing and disseminating research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-review files document the process of improvement and correction that underpins published findings; making them available is framed as integrating that process into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review should improve clarity and robustness of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: These discussions... aim to improve a study’s clarity and the robustness of its conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is described functionally as a months-long conversation intended to strengthen the work; published reports evidence how that strengthening occurred.
